analysis:
Both changed files are CI test scripts. They do not touch provider runtime code, the coordinator-provider protocol, attestation, cache storage or key handling, so I identified no regression against TB-002, TB-011, T-041 or the other cited threats.

scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py (head lines 34-68): the console lane `lint-console` and the CONSOLE expression are replaced by a generic `docs` lane in the test fixtures, and the ROUTED mapping drops the lint-console job. The security-relevant router assertions are unchanged. These cover only exact-label grants, https-only plane contact, fork PRs never contacting the plane, hostile-text sanitisation, read-only permissions with no id-token or secrets, and release/credentialed workflows keeping literal blacksmith runners (UNROUTED). The test now requires ci.yml to define a `docs` job at line 48. That job's existence and the removal of `lint-console` are in workflow files outside the supplied units, so I could not confirm the test matches the real ci.yml. A mismatch would fail CI rather than weaken security.

scripts/test-docs-impact-check.py (head lines 40-78): the "retained console" and "console protocol fixtures" cases are removed, and the retired-mapping test now forbids any rule source pattern starting with admin-ui/, console-ui/, coordinator/ or e2e/. This fits the platform-ownership rescope in the threat model. The change narrows the docs-impact obligations that the rules enforce. docs-impact-rules.json is not in the supplied units, so I cannot confirm that the retained-console rules were removed there. If the rules still exist, the test would fail closed. T-041 references the coordinator's cache_route_keys.go, which is backend-owned. A docs-impact trigger for coordinator files is dropped from this repo, which is a documentation-process change and not a control regression. The `docs-not-needed` maintainer override test is unchanged.

Residual question: the companion workflow and rules changes were not supplied, so test and workflow consistency is unverified.
